entities.summary: Benjamin Rush was an American revolutionary, a Founding Father of the United States and signatory to the U.S. Declaration of Independence, and a civic leader in Philadelphia, where he was a physician, politician, social reformer, humanitarian, educator, and the founder of Dickinson College. Rush was a Pennsylvania delegate to the Continental Congress. He later described his efforts in support of the American Revolution, saying: "He aimed well." He served as Surgeon General of the Middle Department of the Continental Army and became a professor of chemistry, medical theory, and clinical practice at the University of Pennsylvania.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a Founding Father and Surgeon General of the Continental Army, Benjamin Rush played a crucial role in the American Revolution, contributing to the development of medical care and public health policies that shaped the young nation. His legacy as a civic leader and educator continues to influence American society today.
